text: Not All PIPs Was put on a PIP for 3 months, 3 years into my job. Every post I read online said it's over, Paid Interview Period. I vowed that if I get through it, I will post a positive story to this community. This is my hopecore contribution. I had clear metrics to hit, everything was well-documented, and because I was 3 years in, I was very familiar with the workflow and could do really well. My mother died and I fell ill for a while shortly after, which led to my performance dropping. But here I am, 3 months in, feeling great. It wasn't exhausting or draining, mainly because I am lucky to have a fair manager and I simply refused to think about the worst case scenario. Focusing one day at a time, one checkin at a time, one week at a time, and we're 12 weeks down. So for everyone out there: if you're put on a PIP, critically assess if it is in good faith. If yes, go for it guns blazing. A PIP is not a death sentence. An alternate outcome is possible.
label: situation_report
